name: Persepolis
description: Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire, begun by Darius I around 518 BC on the plains of Marvdasht in southern Iran. Its palaces and grand gateways stand on a vast raised terrace against the Zagros Mountains. Visitors can still see stairways carved with processions of gift-bearing delegations, before Alexander the Great's army burned the site in 330 BC.
